title: Tropical Shower Head Repair & Replacement – Sanur Guide
meta: Fix or replace your clogged tropical shower head in a Sanur villa. Step-by-step descaling, replacement tips, and installation advice from a local plumber.
intro: A dripping, low-pressure, or crusty tropical shower head is one of the most common complaints we hear from villa owners here in Sanur. In most cases you can clear the nozzles yourself with a simple vinegar soak; in others the arm, cartridge, or fitting has corroded beyond saving and needs swapping. Below is what to check first, when to call for a replacement, and how to get the new head installed without flooding the bathroom.

paragraphs: Before you reach for a wrench, identify which symptom you are actually dealing with. The fix changes completely depending on where the fault sits.

The most frequent issues in older Sanur villas are: water still trickling after you shut off the tap (a worn cartridge or O-ring), spray that hits only half the tiles (blocked nozzles), a faint metallic taste or brown tint (corroding internal parts), and a shower arm that wobbles or leaks at the ceiling joint.
bullets: Drip after shutoff → cartridge or seal, not the head itself
Uneven or weak spray → limescale inside the face plate
Rusty water or flaking chrome → corrosion of the internal body
Loose or leaking arm → thread damage or missing washer

paragraphs: PDAM mains water in Bali carries a fair amount of dissolved calcium, and the warm, humid air accelerates mineral deposits on every surface it touches. Over six to twelve months the tiny holes in your rain-shower face plate get glazed over with white crust, cutting flow by half or more.

You can usually clear this without replacing anything. Unscrew the head from its arm, fill a bucket or large bowl with white vinegar (or a 1:1 mix of vinegar and water for very heavy scale), and submerge the head overnight. In the morning scrub gently with an old toothbrush, rinse under running water, and reattach. If the nozzles are still restricted, push a pin through each hole while the head is still damp.
bullets: Never use steel wool or abrasive pads on chrome finishes – they scratch and trap moisture that leads to pitting
If you have a pull-out hand shower attached to the same riser, soak both heads together
Repeat the soak every two to three months during the dry season when evaporation speeds up scaling

sections.h2: When to Replace Instead of Repair
paragraphs: Soaking helps only if the internal body is intact. If the plastic housing has cracked, the brass core is pitted green, or the face plate will not seat flat against the cartridge, descaling will give you one good week at best.

Older villas in Sanur were often fitted with budget heads whose cartridges are proprietary. When those wear out, finding a matching replacement can be frustrating. Measure the diameter of the head, note the thread size on the arm (commonly ½-inch BSP), and photograph the whole assembly before ordering. A clear photo sent over WhatsApp lets us confirm compatibility before you spend money on the wrong part.

sections.h2: Choosing the Right Rain Shower for Your Villa
paragraphs: Size matters more than looks. A 30 cm head works well in a compact ensuite; a 40–50 cm panel suits a larger master bathroom but demands adequate pressure from your rooftop tank or pump. If your villa runs off a small PDAM connection with no booster, a very wide head will produce a weak trickle rather than a satisfying rain effect.

Because Sanur sits right on the coast, salt-laden air eats unprotected finishes quickly. Stainless steel or solid-brass bodies with a PVD coating hold up far better than thin chrome-plated plastic. Avoid heads that rely on a single rubber gasket for the entire seal – in humid conditions those degrade within a year or two.

Check whether your existing shower arm is long enough to support the new head's weight without sagging. Heavy glass or metal panels can stress a short, thin arm and eventually crack the ceiling tile above.

sections.h2: Installing a New Tropical Shower Head
paragraphs: Turn off the water at the source: close the valve feeding your rooftop tank, or switch off the well-pump breaker if you run on borehole water. Open the tap briefly to relieve residual pressure before unscrewing anything.

Wrap the male thread of the new head (or the arm, depending on which side has the threads) with four to five turns of PTFE tape, clockwise when looking at the end. Hand-tighten first, then give one firm quarter-turn with pliers protected by a cloth. Overtightening cracks plastic fittings and strips brass threads – both are expensive mistakes in a bathroom where re-access means removing tiles.

Run the water at full flow for a minute, watch the joint from below, and check that spray is even across the whole face. If you see a slow seep at the connection, tighten another eighth of a turn. If it still weeps, shut off, add more tape, and redo the joint rather than forcing it.
During the rainy season be extra careful working under the ceiling: condensation plus a dripping pipe can make the area above slick. Lay down an old towel and keep a bucket handy.

faq.q: How often should I descale my tropical shower head?
faq.a: In Sanur's hard-water, high-humidity climate, a quick vinegar soak every two to three months keeps nozzles clear. If you notice pressure dropping before that interval, do not wait – scale builds up faster once the first layer forms.

faq.q: Can I fit any rain-shower head onto my villa's existing plumbing?
faq.a: Not always. Most Bali villas use ½-inch BSP threads, but older builds sometimes have metric or non-standard fittings. Measure the thread diameter and length, photograph the arm and cartridge, and send those images over WhatsApp so we can confirm the new head will actually screw on without an adapter.

faq.q: My new shower still drips after I turn the tap off. Is it the head?
faq.a: Usually not. A post-shutoff drip points to the diverter valve or the cartridge inside the wall mixer, not the face plate. Replacing the head will not fix it. This is a small internal part swap; if you are not comfortable opening the escutcheon, call us and we can sort it out quickly.

cta: Send a clear photo of your shower head and arm on WhatsApp and we will tell you whether a descale, a cartridge swap, or a full replacement is what you need – no obligation, just a straight answer.
